correctness.rationale: For any genuine primitive two-cycle the first-coordinate recurrence forces alternating nonzero second coordinates ±t. The sum and difference of the two exact second-coordinate equations force first coordinates 2/(1+b)∓t/2 and a necessary-and-sufficient positive-root equation Q(t)=(c-1/2-b/4)t²+at-d-4b/(1+b)²=0. All cases follow from a concave/convex quadratic with negative constant and positive linear coefficients, including the discriminant equality and c=c0 boundary. The one-step Jacobians at y=±t are well defined, and symbolic multiplication confirms the return trace, determinant and exact identity det(I-DF²)=2(1+b)tQ′(t). This identity forces multiplier +1 at double roots and a real >1 multiplier at the larger root. The usual strict Schur conditions apply to the real two-by-two return matrix. The stated rational example checks exactly. The executable checker tests algebraic identities and selected exact-rational cases; proof of all-parameter statements is deductive, not experimental. No higher-period, global-attractor or unit-circle nonlinear stability claim is made.

originality.rationale: The 2019 founding source already contains the map, a fixed-point-free argument and a numerical period-two onset. Inspection of the complete public article, including eq. (1), Section 2.1, Figure 2 and Sections 3–5, found no exact four-parameter period-two count, two coexisting positive roots, finite fold equality, parameter-infinity branch or explicit Schur stability formulas. A similarly titled 2023 FPGA paper treats a one-dimensional piecewise-linear map, so it cannot imply this quadratic planar theorem. Targeted publication-record searches for source aliases, discriminant, two-cycle bifurcations and multipliers found no statement covering the theorem. General polynomial root and Schur techniques are prior mathematical tools, not asserted original innovations. A specialized undiscovered treatment of this exact map remains a publication-priority risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent exact period-two census for this map could exist in unindexed or unidentified specialized literature; publication priority is not independently certified.
The same-model analysis proves only linear attraction in strict Schur regions and does not classify nonlinear dynamics at multiplier boundaries.
This theorem neither guarantees absence of other attractors nor rules out higher-period or chaotic behavior.

value.rationale: The source introduces an unusual planar chaotic map having no equilibrium and observes an initial period-two regime only numerically. For this precise natural object, the primitive two-cycle census and stability become a complete four-parameter structural invariant rather than a table at arbitrary sample parameters. The proof discovers a discriminant-controlled coexistence region, a genuine finite coalescence boundary, and a distinct branch disappearing at infinity, with exact return-multiplier tests and an attracting-vs-unstable coexistence witness. These facts can organize future parameter-bifurcation and basin studies, without requiring a paper-sized theorem or claiming global chaos classification.
